These outstanding mechanical properties were mainly attributed to profuse deformation twinning. Both high strain rate and cryogenic temperature promoted deformation twin- ning.
Grain refinement caused by deformation twinning, dislocation slip and dynamic recrystallisation added to work hardening and the excellent tensile strain.

Based on our structural characterization, some of the nano-grains observed here were very likely caused by DRX. This phenomenon is consistent with the report that TBs can act as preferred zones for DRX [29].

Twins contribute to the mechanical properties of materials because TBs act as barriers for dislocation motion, thus pre- venting high local dislocation concentration during dynamic deformation, and effectively increasing the dislocation storage capability of the materials [30].

While experimental observation of the necking region
revealed that deformation twinning, dislocation accumulation,
grain refinement, and DRX all contributed to the strength and
ductility of the material, deformation twinning was the domi-
nant factor.

The resulting TBs played a critical role in promoting
dislocation accumulation, grain refinement and DRX.

DRX effectively lowers the local dislocation density,
which enables further plastic deformation and thus improves
ductility at high strain rates.

Grain refinement increases strength because GBs act as bar-
riers to the motion of dislocations [36].

High strain
rate restricts the mobility of dislocations and gives less time for
dislocation slip [34].

Although DRX reduces the
dislocation density that leads to softening [29], the resulting nano-
meter grain size strengthens materials through the Hall-Petch
effect.
